findings.text: Parent interest helper reports no interest when child-event flag is absent from the input mask, and otherwise narrows the mask to the subset of events that the framework can deliver with parent and name context.
Event submission helper forwards its group, event and caller merge callback to the central insert path with an empty auxiliary argument.
Overflow path requeues a group-private preallocated overflow event without attempting a merge, while overflow detection is a simple test of the overflow bit in an event mask.
Queue emptiness inspection requires the caller to already hold the group notification lock and reflects whether the pending notification list is empty.

Marks that advertise explicit ignore-flag support use their stored ignore value verbatim; legacy marks always treat directory events as ignored and derive child-ignore interest from the main mask rather than the stored value.

Stored ignore interest is first limited to defined event bits; a candidate mask then applies to directories only when directory interest is present and to parent iteration only when child interest is present.

Effective ignore evaluation returns empty when no ignore bits exist, returns stored event bits directly for plain non-parent cases, and otherwise expands legacy handling and suppresses the result when directory or child applicability fails.

Advertised mark interest starts from the main mask, adds modify interest when ignored state is not configured to survive modifications so clearing can be observed, and unions stored ignore bits so parent traversal can notice child-ignore interest.
Inode-scoped mark helpers provide adding, locked adding and lookup by group, each delegating to the generic object-mark implementation with the inode object type.
Event initialization prepares an empty queue linkage for a new event object, while the unmount helper for inodes performs no action in this configuration.
Verity digest capacity equals the largest supported hash digest size and the verity descriptor is bounded above by sixteen thousand three hundred eighty four bytes.
Filesystem verity integration is a table of six operations covering begin and end of enablement, descriptor retrieval, Merkle page read and readahead, and Merkle block write during construction.

Enable begin and end execute under the inode write semaphore with a possible release between them, descriptor fetch tolerates concurrent callers, and Merkle read and readahead tolerate concurrent callers even on overlapping ranges.

Enablement proceeds from a begin preparation that rejects concurrent enable with busy, through Merkle block writes, to an end step that on success persists a descriptor and marks the inode verity and on failure with absent descriptor performs cleanup only.
When verity support is compiled out, enable, measure and metadata ioctls report operation not supported, digest query reports absence with zero length, and readahead is an empty operation.

Open helper passes through cleanly for non-verity inodes and delegates verity inodes to the internal open path; folio verification delegates to block verification over the full folio extent starting at zero.
Bio verification and zero-hash fill helpers in this configuration trigger a one-time warning, indicating they must not be reached when verity is disabled.
Early boot code, data and read-only data are placed in dedicated init sections with cold and stack protections for code, while exit data and exit-call pointers use dedicated exit sections.

Reference and memory-init annotations select reference or init sections or expand to nothing depending on configuration, with matching assembly directives for head, init and reference text, data and read-only data plus previous-section closers.

Kernel parameter registration centers on a descriptor holding a name string, a setup callback and an early flag; registration either emits aligned init strings and descriptors in the setup section or expands to nothing when disabled.

Ordered boot hooks progress from early through pure, core, postcore, arch, subsystem, filesystem, root filesystem, device and late levels with synchronous companions, plus device as the default level, exit-call registration and a separate console hook.

Init and exit callables are parameterless functions returning status or nothing; stored entries hold either a relative offset converted via helper or a direct pointer, with unique naming derived from module, counter, line and function and per-level sections.
Initial task command name is the swapper label, previous cputime initialization either installs an unlocked raw lock or expands empty, and initial thread info resides in its dedicated data section.
Initial ram disk reservation and ramfs wait helpers are empty inline operations that return immediately in this configuration.
Mapping extent kinds are numbered sequentially from zero for hole, delayed allocation, mapped, unwritten and inline data.

Mapping flags occupy successive single-bit positions from the lowest bit upward for new, dirty, shared, merged, buffer-head, extended attribute, boundary, anonymous write, atomic bio, integrity, zero tail, verity, private, folio batch, size changed and stale indications, with buffer-head and integrity collapsing to zero when disabled.

Mapping descriptor carries disk address and file offset and length, a numeric type and flags, block and dax device pointers, inline data and private pointers, and a validity cookie, with all-ones address denoting invalid.

Sector translation adds the distance from mapping start to the disk base and converts to sector units, returning an all-ones sentinel for anonymous writes, while inline access offsets into the embedded data area by the same distance.
Each header uses a distinct inclusion guard macro, with the mapping header guard carrying a numeric value.
Exit-use annotation expands either to empty or to a retention marker depending on configuration.
